In what year was SARS-CoV-2 discovered?
SARS-CoV-2: The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
Furosemide: Pfizer. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
In which country is Māori language?
Māori language: New Zealand. The southernmost member of the Austronesian language family, it is related to Cook Islands Māori, Tuamotuan, and Tahitian.
Who is credited with discovering Infrared?
Infrared: William Herschel. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Who is credited with discovering Cherenkov radiation?
Cherenkov radiation: Sergey Vavilov. A classic example of Cherenkov radiation is the characteristic blue glow of an underwater nuclear reactor.
Who is credited with discovering Argon?
Argon: William Ramsay. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Made of adenine bonded to a sugar, this RNA building block underlies ATP, the cell's main energy currency, and doubles as an IV treatment for certain cardiac arrhythmias — what is it?
Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
This white crystalline chemical compound is mainly used as a high-nitrogen agricultural fertilizer, but is also a key ingredient in explosive mixtures used for mining and quarrying — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate is a chemical compound with the formula NH4NO3.
The 16th-largest family of flowering plants, this aromatic group includes cumin, fennel, and coriander alongside deadly relatives like water hemlock — which family?
Apiaceae is a family of mostly aromatic flowering plants named after the type genus Apium, and commonly known as the celery, carrot, or parsley family, or simply as umbellifers.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.
This brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal can develop a vividly iridescent, rainbow-colored surface from thin-film oxidation when heated. What element is it?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
One of only two elements liquid at room temperature, this reddish-brown, pungent-smelling element takes its name from the Greek word for 'stench.' What element is it (symbol Br)?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
Along with the bonobo, which great ape of equatorial Africa's forests and savannas is humans' closest living relative, according to DNA and fossil evidence?
Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.

Making up 25 to 35 percent of protein content in mammals, this triple-helix structural protein is the main component of the extracellular matrix in cartilage, bone, tendons, and skin — name the protein?
Collagen is the main structural protein in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues of many animals.
This breaded, deep-fried snack binds a thick sauce like béchamel with fillings such as meat, seafood, or cheese, and was originally a way to use up leftovers — what is it?
Croquette is a deep-fried roll originating in French cuisine and most extended in Spanish cuisine consisting of a thick binder combined with a filling, which is then breaded.
Mother of Princess Alia, this royal later remarried a senior PLO official in 1970 after her short-lived marriage to Jordan's king ended — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid (15 December 1929 - 21 August 2019) was a Hashemite princess and Queen of Jordan from 1955 until 1957 as the first wife of King Hussein.
Discovered to have two undescribed relatives only in 2019, this Amazonian 'knifefish' is best known for generating powerful electric discharges — which species?
Electrophorus electricus is the best-known species of electric eel. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
Aerobic exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all induce this intense feeling of well-being — which is also, less happily, a symptom of mania — what state is it?
Euphoria (yoo-) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
Madagascar's largest carnivore, this slender, long-tailed mammal evolved cougar-like features independently and climbs trees head-first thanks to flexible ankles — what is it?
Fossa (animal) (Cryptoprocta ferox; FOSS- or) is a slender, long-tailed, cat-like mammal that is endemic to Madagascar.
This flowering plant genus, whose name derives from the Latin word for a small sword, belongs to the iris family and is centered on the Cape Floristic Region of South Africa — which genus?
Gladiolus (from Latin, the diminutive of gladius, a sword) is a genus of perennial cormous flowering plants in the iris family (Iridaceae).
These seed-loving rodents come in 19 species, the golden or Syrian variety being the one most often found in a child's bedroom cage — what are they?
Hamster are rodents (order Rodentia) belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae, which contains 19 species classified in seven genera.

Despite resembling a common shellfish, this ancient arthropod is actually a chelicerate more closely related to spiders and scorpions, and is often called a 'living fossil' for its unchanged ancient body plan — what is it?
Horseshoe crab are arthropods of the family Limulidae and the only surviving xiphosurans.
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length is often understood as roughly the width of a human thumb — name the unit?
Inch (symbol: in or) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
This self-described 'constitutional law attorney' joined Trump's inner circle in November 2019, though reporters found she'd never argued a federal case — who is she?
Jenna Ellis (born November 1, 1984) is an American conservative suspended lawyer who was a member of Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign's legal team.

First described in 1845 by a German physicist, these two fundamental equalities govern how current and voltage behave in an electrical network, building on Georg Ohm's earlier work — what are they called?
Kirchhoff's circuit laws are two equalities that deal with the current and potential difference (commonly known as voltage) in the lumped element model of electrical circuits.
A Ming-dynasty naturalist poured 27 years into a sprawling pharmacology compendium of nearly 1,900 entries, 11,000 prescriptions, and over a thousand herbs — who was this herbalist and physician?
Li Shizhen (July 3, 1518 - 1593), courtesy name Dongbi, was a Chinese acupuncturist, herbalist, naturalist, pharmacologist, physician, and writer of the Ming dynasty.
About 90% of its cases fall into the non-Hodgkin variety, and its tell-tale signs include painless swollen lymph nodes and night sweats — which group of white-blood-cell cancers is this?
Lymphoma is a group of blood and lymph tumors that develop from lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German theoretical physicist is considered the originator of quantum theory and one of the founders of modern physics — who is he?
Max Planck (23 April 1858 - 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
Widowed in 2021, this Israeli-American billionaire physician publishes Israel Hayom and has been among the most prominent financial supporters of a US president since 2016 — who is she?
Miriam Adelson (ne Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
Also called the coypu, this plant-eating rodent digs streamside burrows and now troubles several countries as an invasive species far from its South American home — what is it?
Nutria (Myocastor coypus) is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent from South America.

Covered in large protective keratin scales, these mammals — sometimes called scaly anteaters — range across Asia and sub-Saharan Africa and are the only mammal order known to have such scales — what are they?
Pangolin are mammals of the order Pholidota. The one extant family, the Manidae, has three genera: Manis, Phataginus, and Smutsia.
A self-described socialist active in Finland's Pirate Party, this entrepreneur co-founded a famous file-sharing search engine and later started the privacy service Njalla — who is he?
Peter Sunde (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
Emerging roughly 203 million years ago and wiped out alongside the dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this order of long-necked marine reptiles ruled Jurassic seas — what were they?
Plesiosaur are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
The only member of the genus Rangifer, this circumpolar deer of the Arctic tundra goes by another name entirely in North America — what is it?
Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.
A botanist active in Japan's Meiji era, this scholar died in 1899 after decades of scientific work — who was he?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (October 13, 1851 - August 8, 1899) was a Japanese botanist during the Meiji era.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Known in Hispanic America as guanábana and easily killed by a touch of frost, which Annona fruit blends flavors of strawberry, apple, and sour citrus?
Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanbana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
The only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands, found on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after its Bali and Javan cousins went extinct in the 20th century — what is it?
Sumatran tiger is a population of Panthera tigris sondaica on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.

Governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work and temperature to energy and entropy, this branch of physics underpins chemical, mechanical and biochemical engineering alike — which field of physics?
Thermodynamics is a branch of physics that deals with heat, work, and temperature, and their relation to energy, entropy, and the physical properties of matter and radiation.
Several highly prized truffle species belong to this fungal genus, whose lineage is estimated to date to the close of the Jurassic period — which genus?
Tuber (fungus) is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

Commanding the first spaceflight to carry multiple crew members in 1964, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first human to die during a space mission when his capsule's parachute failed on reentry in 1967 — who was he?
Vladimir Komarov (16 March 1927 - 24 April 1967) was a Soviet test pilot, aerospace engineer, and cosmonaut.

This Polish-American scholar served as Jimmy Carter's national security advisor from 1977 to 1981 and helped organize an influential international policy group known as the Trilateral Commission — who is he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski (March 28, 1928 - May 26, 2017) was a Polish-American diplomat and political scientist.
Marked by inadequate cortisol and aldosterone production in the adrenal glands, this rare, long-term endocrine disorder is also known as primary adrenal insufficiency — what is it?
Addison's disease: Endocrine disorder. Addison's disease arises when the adrenal gland does not produce sufficient amounts of the steroid hormones cortisol and (sometimes) aldosterone.
His mother and wife were both deaf, which steered this Scottish-born inventor toward hearing devices — and, in 1876, the first U.S. patent for the telephone. Who was he?
Alexander Graham Bell: Inventor of the telephone (1847–1922)

These coiled-shelled cephalopods, more closely related to octopuses than to nautiluses despite the resemblance, thrived from the Devonian until vanishing around the dinosaur extinction 66 million years ago — what are they?
Ammonoidea: Extinct subclass of cephalopod molluscs.
Shed and regrown every year on most male deer, this bony head growth serves as both a weapon and a symbol of sexual attraction — what is it?
Antler: Skull projections found in deer.

A physician who began writing stories while studying medicine in Edinburgh, he was knighted in 1902 and created both a famous consulting detective and the dinosaur-filled adventure The Lost World. Who was he?
Arthur Conan Doyle: British writer and physician (1859–1930)
This Indian jurist studied economics at Columbia and the London School of Economics before becoming the chief architect of his country's constitution. Who was he?
B. R. Ambedkar: Indian jurist, economist, politician and social reformer (1891–1956)

This Swiss-American engineer was the only one of a famous physicist's three known biological grandsons to survive childhood, and later earned patents in electronics while working at Texas Instruments — who was he?

Developed to supplement the 727 on short routes, this narrow-body twinjet kept the 707's fuselage width and six-abreast seating and entered service with Lufthansa in 1968 — which best-selling aircraft is it?
Patented by Roche in 1961 and approved for medical use in 1974, which benzodiazepine, similar in effect to diazepam, is sometimes given as a presurgical sedative in 1.5, 3, or 6 mg tablets?
Bromazepam: Benzodiazepine drug. Bromazepam, sold under many brand names, is a benzodiazepine.
First synthesized in 1950 by bombarding curium with alpha particles, this actinide element bears the symbol Cf and is named for a US university and state — what is it?
Californium: Chemical element with atomic number 98 (Cf)
Known also as yoke elm, this species of hornbeam native to Western Asia and Europe grows only up to elevations of about 1,000 metres — which species?
Carpinus betulus: Species of tree. It requires a warm climate for good growth, and occurs only at elevations up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft).
Also known as silver beet or perpetual spinach, this leafy green shares its species with beetroot — which vegetable?
Chard: Green leafy vegetable. Chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris, Cicla Group and Flavescens Group) is a green leafy vegetable.
Sold under the brand name Celexa, this SSRI antidepressant treats major depressive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, and social anxiety — what is it?
Citalopram: SSRI antidepressant. Citalopram, sold under the brand name Celexa among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
Son of a bass-baritone and born into a family of engineers, this American built his first car at 19, won four F1 Grands Prix, and took Le Mans in 1967 — who was he?
Dan Gurney: American racing driver, engineer and motorsport executive (1931–2018)
Nicknamed 'dumb cane' because its poisonous sap can temporarily rob you of speech, this shade-tolerant tropical houseplant is native to the New World — which genus?
Dieffenbachia: Genus of plants. Dieffenbachia, commonly known as dumb cane or leopard lily, is a genus of tropical flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.

The heaviest aircraft ever built by its Brazilian manufacturer, this twin-engine jet transport was developed as a derivative of a regional jetliner, similar in role to the C-130 Hercules. Which aircraft?
Embraer C-390 Millennium: Brazilian military transport aircraft/tanker.
The simplest alkene and the most-produced organic compound on Earth, this colorless gas is also a natural plant hormone used to ripen fruit — what is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
The tallest land animal alive and the largest ruminant on Earth, its closest living relative is the okapi — which long-necked African mammal is it?

After proving a 20-year-old open problem in Riemannian geometry known as the soul conjecture, this reclusive Russian mathematician later quit the field entirely and now lives in seclusion in Saint Petersburg — who is he?
Grown as deciduous shrubs across the temperate Northern Hemisphere and related to the birch family, this plant produces a popular round brown nut — which plant genus?
This branch of biology studies the microscopic structure of tissues, historically distinguished from cytology (the study of cells) and organology (the study of organs) — what is it called?
Histology: Study of the microscopic anatomy of cells and tissues of plants and animals.
This nearly worldwide genus of flowering plants — commonly called St. John's wort — was the subject of a definitive taxonomic monograph identifying 36 sections within it. Which genus?
Hypericum: Genus of flowering plants known as St. John's worts.
This Belgian-American physicist-mathematician is best known for wavelets that revolutionized image compression — a family of them even bears her name; who is she?
Ingrid Daubechies: Belgian physicist and mathematician (born 1954)
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
This group of three genetic conditions causes nervous-system tumors; its first type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis, while its second causes early hearing loss — what's it called?
Neurofibromatosis: Three genetic disorders involving benign tumors of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.

He dreamed up an "impossible" triangle, traded ideas with M. C. Escher, and shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for proving black holes are a robust prediction of general relativity — who is this English mathematician?
Roger Penrose: English mathematician, mathematical physicist (born 1931)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Named in 1842 from Brazilian fossils and often called a saber-toothed tiger despite no close kinship to true tigers, this genus of prehistoric predator roamed the Americas until the early Holocene — which animal?
Smilodon: Extinct genus of saber-toothed cat.
It's the largest order of reptiles — lizards and snakes alike — set apart by horny scales they periodically shed and a hinged upper jaw that lets snakes gape around big prey. Which order?
Squamata: Order of reptiles. The now-extinct mosasaurs reached lengths over 14 m (46 ft).
This tangy reddish spice, made from a shrub in the cashew family, is a staple of Arab cuisine and holds symbolic significance on the Haft-sin table at Persian New Year — what is it?
Sumac: Related species of plants in the family Anacardiaceae.
Prized for its durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood with a leather-like smell when freshly milled is a top choice for boat building — what is it?
Teak: Tree species native to South and Southeast Asia.
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.
Known as a noxious weed for its spiky, woody burs that can puncture bare feet and even bicycle tires, this invasive desert-loving plant is native to Eurasia and Africa — name the species?
Tribulus terrestris: Species of flowering plant. Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
Usually appearing on the hands and feet due to a human papillomavirus infection, this benign skin growth typically clears on its own within months to years — what is this common growth called?
Wart: Small, rough growth resembling a cauliflower or a solid blister.
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.

What is the chemical symbol for krypton?
The symbol for krypton is Kr. Krypton is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

In what year was Julie Andrews born?
Julie Andrews: Dame Julie Andrews (born Julia Elizabeth Wells, 1 October 1935) is an English actress, singer and author.
In what year was Kristen Bell born?

In what year was Kelsey Grammer born?
Kelsey Grammer: Allen Kelsey Grammer (born February 21, 1955) is an American actor.
In what year was Jada Pinkett Smith born?
Jada Pinkett Smith: Jada Koren Pinkett Smith (née Pinkett; born September 18, 1971) is an American actress, businesswoman, talk show host and singer.
In what year was Kerry Von Erich born?
Kerry Von Erich: Kerry Gene Adkisson (February 3, 1960 – February 18, 1993), better known by his ring name Kerry Von Erich, was an American professional wrestler.
In what year was Elvis Presley born?
Elvis Presley: Elvis Aaron Presley (January 8, 1935 – August 16, 1977) was an American singer and actor.

Caitlyn Jenner: Caitlyn Marie Jenner (born William Bruce Jenner, October 28, 1949), is an American media personality and retired Olympic gold medal-winning decathlete.

Sean Penn: Sean Justin Penn (born August 17, 1960) is an American actor and filmmaker.

Kenneth Branagh: Sir Kenneth Charles Branagh ( BRAN-ə; born 10 December 1960) is a British actor and filmmaker.

Burt Reynolds: Burton Leon Reynolds Jr. (February 11, 1936 – September 6, 2018) was an American actor.
In what year did Cary Grant die?
